column4: Records the method used to confirm the patient's HIV-positive status — either a Rapid Test (TR) or PCR. Auto-filled from the ATS module if a positive result already exists.
The calendar date on which the HIV-positive result was confirmed. Auto-filled from the ATS module if available.
Records where the HIV-positive test was performed — either at a health unit (US) or at a community testing site (ATS-C).
For children under 18 months, records the date on which a clinical presumptive diagnosis of HIV was made, prior to confirmatory PCR testing.
Result of the first PCR test for HIV in infants. Auto-filled from the CCR/Lab module if a result already exists in the system.
Date on which the first PCR test was performed.
Result of a second PCR test performed when the first result was discordant or inconclusive.
Date on which the second discordant PCR test was performed.
For paediatric cases, the clinical or age criterion used to confirm the definitive HIV diagnosis.

column3: Has the Patient Taken ARVs Before?
column4: Screens whether the patient has previously received any antiretroviral drugs, including PrEP, PEP, PMTCT, or earlier treatment episodes. A Yes response enables the 'Types of ARVs Taken' field.
Specifies the category of ARVs previously received by the patient before the current ART enrolment episode.

column3: Has the Patient Ever Been to an ART Clinic?
column4: For transferred patients, records whether the patient has a prior history of attending an ART clinic, triggering display of previous clinical summary fields.
Most recent CD4 absolute count recorded at the previous ART clinic, used to assess immune status at entry.
Most recent CD4 percentage from the previous ART clinic. Mutually exclusive with absolute CD4 and semi-quantitative CD4.
Categorised CD4 count when an absolute value is unavailable, indicating whether the count was ≤200 or >200 cells/mm³.
The date on which the most recent CD4 test was performed at the previous facility.
Most recent quantitative HIV viral load result from the previous ART clinic, expressed as copies/mL.
Qualitative viral load category when a numeric value is unavailable — either Undetectable or Less Than (<) a specified threshold.
column6: Undetectable or Less Than (<) a specified threshold

column4: The numeric threshold used when qualitative VL is reported as 'less than' a value (e.g., <20 copies/mL).
The date on which the most recent viral load was measured at the previous facility.
The tuberculosis preventive therapy regimen that the patient was last receiving, used to determine TPT history and continuation needs.
The date on which the patient began the most recently recorded TPT regimen. Must be ≥ date of birth.
The date on which the patient completed or stopped the most recently recorded TPT regimen. Must be ≥ Start Date.
The date the patient first entered HIV pre-ART care, used to calculate time from HIV diagnosis to ART initiation.
Name of the health unit where the patient first enrolled in HIV care, prior to transfer.
The department or sector within the originating facility where the patient received HIV care.
The date on which the patient first initiated antiretroviral therapy. Must be ≥ date of birth.
The name of the health unit at which the patient first commenced antiretroviral treatment.
The first ART regimen the patient received when initiating treatment. Selected from the national formulary regimen list.
The WHO HIV clinical staging at the time treatment was started, used for baseline immunological status characterisation.
Documents whether the patient was pregnant at the time antiretroviral therapy was initiated.
Documents whether the patient was breastfeeding at the time of ART initiation, relevant for PMTCT regimen selection.
The absolute CD4 cell count at the time ART was initiated, used to characterise baseline immunological status.
The CD4 percentage at ART initiation. Mutually exclusive with absolute CD4 and semi-quantitative options.
Categorised CD4 count at ART initiation when a precise value is unavailable.
Records any regimen substitutions within the first line of ART, for example due to toxicity, drug interactions, or pregnancy. Up to 3 entries permitted.
The clinical justification for substituting within the first ART line.
The date on which each first-line alternative regimen was started.
Records any change to a second-line ART regimen, typically due to confirmed therapeutic failure. Up to 2 entries permitted.
The clinical justification for escalating to a second-line ART regimen.
The date on which the patient was switched to a second-line ART regimen.
Records a change to a third-line ART regimen, reserved for confirmed multi-drug resistance or failure of second-line therapy.
The clinical justification for escalating to a third-line ART regimen.
The date on which the patient was switched to a third-line ART regimen.
The patient's primary presenting concern or reason for attending the ART consultation, recorded in their own words.
A structured narrative of the patient's current clinical problems, symptoms, and relevant events since the last consultation.

Displays all allergies previously recorded in the system for this patient. Allows addition of new allergies. On initial consultation, shown inline in the flow; on follow-up, accessible via the right sidebar menu.
Sexually transmitted infection screening using the standardised STI screening protocol. Captures symptoms and diagnosis for syndromic STI management.
Screening for cervical cancer using VIA (visual inspection with acetic acid) or cytology, per the standardised CACUM screening protocol.
Screening for diabetes mellitus using fasting blood glucose or random blood glucose, per the standardised diabetes screening protocol.
Tuberculosis symptom screening using the standardised TB screening algorithm, capturing cough, weight loss, fever, and night sweats.
Blood pressure-based hypertension screening using the standardised HTA screening protocol.
Displays all chronic conditions or significant medical diagnoses previously recorded in the system. Allows addition of new conditions during the consultation.
Captures menstrual cycle information relevant to HIV care, including cycle regularity and last menstrual period. Shown only for female patients aged 10 years and older.
The contraceptive method(s) currently being used or chosen by the patient, recorded to support reproductive health within HIV care.
Free text field for specifying a family planning method not covered by the standard options.

Auto-displays any vital signs already recorded for this patient on the same day, allowing editing. Captures temperature, blood pressure, pulse rate, and respiratory rate per the standard vital signs form.
The patient's measured body weight, auto-displayed if already entered on the same day and editable.
The patient's height. On initial consultation, always captured. On follow-up, for patients ≥18 years, auto-populated from the most recent consultation and editable.
Body Mass Index auto-calculated from weight and height. A value <16 kg/m² is listed as a danger/warning sign in the Master Record.
Mid-upper arm circumference for nutritional assessment, used to classify acute malnutrition especially when weight/height are unreliable.
Composite nutritional status classification based on BMI, MUAC, and clinical assessment, following the national nutritional assessment protocol.
Clinician's overall descriptive assessment of the patient's appearance, comfort, and distress level at the time of consultation.
Standardised assessment of the patient's alertness and neurological responsiveness (e.g., Alert, Voice, Pain, Unresponsive). An altered level of consciousness is a documented danger sign.
Structured body-systems physical examination. On initial consultation, shown inline in the flow; on follow-up, available via the right sidebar menu only.
Standardised neurological assessment including motor function, reflexes, and cognition. On initial consultation, shown inline; on follow-up, accessible via the sidebar menu.
ICD-10 or SNOMED coded diagnoses recorded during the consultation, including opportunistic infections, comorbidities, and HIV-related conditions.

The patient's current WHO HIV clinical stage (I–IV), which determines treatment eligibility and clinical urgency. Required field. On follow-up, auto-populated from the previous consultation and editable.
Assessment of the patient's adherence to their antiretroviral regimen, classified as Good, At-Risk, or Poor based on the clinician's evaluation and patient-reported pill-taking behaviour.

Captures any adverse reactions or side effects experienced by the patient in relation to their ART regimen. On initial consultation, shown only for transferred patients. On follow-up, shown for all patients and auto-populated from the previous consultation.

Records which Differentiated Service Model(s) the patient is eligible for, determining their care delivery modality and follow-up frequency. Multiple models may be assigned. On follow-up, auto-populated and editable.
The current status of each assigned Differentiated Service Model — whether the patient is starting, continuing, or ending that model.
Free text description for a differentiated service model not covered by the standard MDS list.

Records whether chemotherapy for Kaposi's sarcoma has been indicated for this patient. Displayed only for patients enrolled in the DAH (Advanced HIV Disease) differentiated service model with status Start or Continue.
The sequential cycle number of Kaposi's sarcoma chemotherapy being administered. Each cycle number can only be selected once per patient record.
The date on which the current chemotherapy cycle commenced.
The date on which the current chemotherapy cycle was completed.
The specific chemotherapy regimen used for Kaposi's sarcoma treatment, selected from approved national regimens.
Free text description for a Kaposi's sarcoma chemotherapy regimen not covered by the standard options.
The type or purpose of this APSS&PP session, classified as a Normal/routine visit, Absent (missed appointment follow-up), Restart (return after interruption), or AMA (Adherence Strengthening).
column6: Normal/routine visit, Absent (missed appointment follow-up), Restart (return after interruption), or AMA (Adherence Strengthening).

column4: Records whether the patient has accepted their HIV-positive diagnosis. Shown only during the first two APSS&PP appointments, as part of ART preparation counselling.
Documents whether the patient understands the importance and benefits of commencing antiretroviral therapy. Shown only during the first two APSS&PP appointments.
Records whether the counsellor discussed the benefits of having a trusted support person involved in the patient's care and treatment. Shown only during the first two APSS&PP appointments.
Free text notes from the counsellor about the content of the ART preparation counselling session, including any key concerns raised.

column3: Date Patient Ready to Start ART
column4: The date on which the patient indicated they are psychosocially ready to commence antiretroviral therapy, as determined through the counselling process.

column3: Are There Psychosocial Factors Affecting Adherence?
column4: Screening question to determine whether any psychosocial barrier to ART adherence is present. A Yes response triggers display of the detailed psychosocial factors list.
Multi-select list of specific psychosocial, social, or structural barriers that may prevent or reduce the patient's adherence to ART. Enables targeted counselling and referral planning.
Records whether the child's caregiver(s) have given consent for the child's HIV diagnosis to be disclosed to the child. Required step in the paediatric and adolescent disclosure process.
The current stage of HIV diagnosis disclosure to the child or adolescent — whether no disclosure has occurred, partial disclosure, or full disclosure has been completed.
column6: no disclosure has occurred, partial disclosure, or full disclosure has been completed.

column3: Child Knows Own Name and Caregivers' Names
column4: Developmental readiness assessment: documents whether the child can identify themselves and their caregivers by name, a prerequisite for disclosure.
Developmental readiness: documents whether the child can independently manage personal hygiene tasks (bathing, teeth, hair), indicating readiness for increased health responsibility.

column3: Child Can Explain Importance of Daily Medication
column4: Assesses whether the child understands and can explain why taking medication every day without fail is important for their health.

column3: Child Knows Medication Timing and Dosage
column4: Assesses whether the child knows the specific details of their medication schedule — the time and dose to take each day.

column3: Child Receives Caregiver Support for Medication and Visits
column4: Documents whether the child receives adequate support from their caregivers to take medication consistently and attend health facility appointments.

column3: Caregivers Understand Advantages of Starting RDT
column4: Records whether the primary and secondary caregivers have been informed of and understand the benefits of initiating the child's HIV treatment (RDT).

column3: 1st and 2nd Caregivers Prepared to Start RDT
column4: Documents whether both primary and secondary caregivers are emotionally and practically prepared for the child to begin HIV treatment.
Records the counsellor's assessment of whether the patient (child or adolescent) themselves is psychologically ready to commence HIV treatment.
Documents the planned disclosure method — whether the diagnosis will be revealed by a caregiver or by a health care provider.
Documents the planned disclosure setting — whether at home or at the health facility.
The planned calendar date on which the HIV diagnosis will be disclosed to the child or adolescent.
The specific key population group(s) to which the patient belongs, used to tailor HIV prevention, care, and support services. MSM option hidden for female patients.
The current enrolment status within the key population programme for each identified group.
Records whether lubricants and/or condoms were provided to the patient during the consultation, an essential harm reduction intervention.

column3: PP1 – Sexual Behaviour & Safe Sex / Condom Provision
column4: Records whether counselling on safe sexual behaviour and condom use was provided during this session.

column3: PP2 – Serostatus Disclosure to Partner & Partner Testing
column4: Records whether counselling on disclosing HIV status to the sexual partner and inviting the partner for HIV testing was conducted.

column3: PP3 – Importance of Adherence to Pre-ART and ART
column4: Records whether counselling on the importance of adhering to both pre-ART care and ART treatment was provided.
Records whether STI prevention and treatment counselling was conducted during this session.

column3: PP5 – Family Planning, Safe Pregnancy & PMTCT
column4: Records whether counselling on family planning, safe pregnancy, and PMTCT was provided.

column3: PP6 – Alcohol and Other Drug Use
column4: Records whether counselling on the impact of alcohol and drug use on ART adherence and HIV progression was conducted.

column3: PP7 – Referral to Community Support Services
column4: Records whether the patient was referred or linked to community support services such as social protection, food programmes, or peer support.

column3: Has Patient Disclosed Serostatus to Anyone?
column4: Records whether the patient has informed any person in their life about their HIV-positive status, which is a key indicator of psychosocial readiness and support.
The relationship of the person the patient has chosen to disclose their HIV status to, enabling assessment of social support networks.

column3: All Contacts with Unknown Serostatus Tested?
column4: Records whether all contacts of the patient (sexual partners, needle-sharing partners, children <15, parents of children ≤15) with unknown HIV status have been tested.
For children, adolescents, elderly patients, and those with physical or mental disability, documents the name of the person responsible for administering the patient's ARV medication.
The relationship of the caregiver who administers the patient's ARV drugs to the patient.
The number of ART doses the patient reports having missed in the 14 days prior to the consultation. Used to calculate the adherence percentage.
Calculated adherence category based on the proportion of doses taken: Good (>87%), At-Risk (78–87%), or Poor (<78%). Calculated as (doses taken ÷ doses prescribed) × 100.
The calculated percentage of prescribed doses that the patient actually took over the last 2 weeks.
The number of days by which the patient was late for their scheduled clinical appointment. Used to identify appointment adherence patterns.

column3: Delay in ARV Collection at Pharmacy (days)
column4: The number of days by which the patient was late collecting their antiretroviral medication from the pharmacy. Indicates pharmacy-level adherence.
Records whether the patient is following their individualised adherence plan, covering correct dosing schedule, timing, and what to do if doses are missed or during travel.

column3: Can Health Unit Service Be Improved?
column4: Asks the patient for their feedback on the quality of services received at the health unit, supporting patient-centred quality improvement.
The specific area(s) the patient identifies for improving the health unit's service, used to inform quality improvement plans.
The specific reason(s) why this patient requires an Adherence Strengthening (AMA) session. Guides the content and intensity of adherence support interventions.
The specific intervention(s) or strategies selected as part of the patient's personalised adherence plan, addressing the identified barriers and reasons for poor adherence.
Records enrolment status in the Mother-to-Mother support group, which provides peer support for HIV-positive mothers on ART.
Records enrolment status in the Parents and Caregivers support group, for caregivers of HIV-positive children.
Records enrolment status in the support group for children and adolescents whose HIV diagnosis has been fully disclosed to them.

column3: Support Group – Peer Education / Mentor Mother (MM)
column4: Records enrolment status in the Peer Education Mentor Mother programme, where experienced HIV-positive mothers support newly diagnosed mothers.

column3: Support Group – Peer Education / Adolescent & Youth (AJM)
column4: Records enrolment status in the Adolescent and Youth peer education programme for HIV-positive young people.
Records enrolment status in the Champion Man peer education programme, engaging HIV-positive men as peer educators and advocates.
Free text description for any support group the patient is enrolled in that is not covered by the standard list.

Records whether the clinician suspects that the patient's current ART regimen is failing to suppress viral load, based on clinical and/or laboratory criteria. A Yes response triggers submission to the Therapeutic Committee. The system preserves all historical entries for audit.
The unique identifier assigned to the case when submitted to the multi-disciplinary Therapeutic Committee for review and approval of a line change.
The date on which the Therapeutic Committee formally approved the recommended ART regimen change for this patient.
Classifies the type of regimen modification — either a substitution within the same ART line (Alternative) or an escalation to a higher ART line (Line Change).

column3: Reason for Alternative or Line Change
column4: The clinical justification for the regimen modification. Toxicity and side effects, therapeutic failure, pregnancy, initiation of TB treatment, or another reason.
Free text description for the regimen change reason when 'Other' is selected from the standard justification list.
